Thank you, Chair. My name is Alexa Dominique. I'm here on behalf of the DMUN Foundation. I'm also the UNA-USA Global Goals Ambassador. I would like to commend the subcommittee for presenting a well-structured and forward-looking work plan. The focus on practical guidance, data-informed policymaking, and administrative integration provides a strong foundation for this work. We would like to offer several recommendations. First, regarding the conceptual framework, it may be useful to clearly position tax policy as one instrument within a broader economic policy toolkit. From an effective perspective, not all distributional challenges are best addressed through tax design alone. Clarifying where tax measures are most effective and where complementary policies may be more appropriate can help ensure that intervention— interventions remain efficient and fiscally sustainable. Second, on the informal economy, the focus on inclusion is particularly important. It may be valuable to emphasize incentive-based approaches that encourage gradual formalization, such as simplified regimes, reduced compliance costs, and improve access to services. Policies that balance revenue objectives with economic participation can help expand the tax base while supporting long-term growth. Third, with respect to the proposed administrative toolkit, integrating a gender perspective into tax administration processes should be approached through operational practicality and scalability. This could include incorporating gender considerations into taxpayer services, audit selection criteria, and institutional practices while ensuring that implementation remains feasible within existing administrative capacities. Fourth, on tax data, the emphasis on improving data collection and analysis is critical. From a policy design perspective, better data enables more precise targeting and evaluation of outcomes. Strengthening data systems, including disaggregation where appropriate, can improve both policy effectiveness and resource allocation decisions over time. Finally, regarding international taxation, a clear understanding of how cross-border tax rules may influence economic outcomes could support a more coherent policy design. Ensuring consistency across domestic and international frameworks may help reduce unintended distortions and improve overall system efficiency. Overall, this work presents an important opportunity to strengthen tax systems in a way that is economically sound, administratively practical, and supported by robust data, while remaining adoptable across different contexts. In doing so, it could help support women's participation and inclusion in economic activity. We thank you.
Thank you. Guidre, please.
